data.why: The shipped app only loads data by having its server clone a GitHub URL at runtime (requests.get to api.github.com plus `git clone`), but the sandboxed server has no network once it starts, so that path can never succeed; seed/app.py is a minimally patched copy of app.py that adds a 'Load bundled example database' button pointing at the app's own folder, and the seeded lab_database/experiment_database/publication_database YAML files (matching the exact schema load_dataset expects, including a missing catalog_id, an unvalidated antibody, an empty-tube siRNA, and a missing-publication cell line) land next to app.py so that button has real records to show.

goals: find which antibodies against a given protein target are in stock, validated, and at what dilution for a specific application
check whether a cell line has documented STR authentication and its source publication before using it in an experiment
locate an experiment's raw data folder and hard drive, and see which cell lines, conditions, and microscope were used
filter reagents (plasmids, dyes, small molecules, siRNAs) by storage location and reorder status to plan lab inventory
select a set of records matching a search or filter and export them as CSV or PDF for a materials-and-methods section or lab meeting

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-organised tree of a read-only lab-database browser: the phases follow real lab work, the general labels are free of tool names, and nine of the ten screens I checked show what their nodes claim. Before filing it needs fixes: the antibody-dilution gap is misdiagnosed (the app defines the columns but its loader drops them), the Publications-to-experiments link is hidden inside a Mobile-view task whose screen doesn't show Mobile view, and the display phase is thin.
